summary: Backend API tested end-to-end via pytest. Created /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with 24 tests covering auth, agency, companies CRUD/search/filters, IRMS PIB lookup, employees CRUD, templates listing (57 templates verified), document generation + download with JWT token, PDV/IOPPD tracking, and dashboard stats. Found and fixed 1 bug: PUT /api/agency returned 500 (MongoDB _id mutation issue). After fix: 24/24 tests passing.

minor.issue: Returns 403 instead of 401 when Authorization header missing. This is FastAPI HTTPBearer default; consider auto_error=False + explicit 401 for cleaner API contract.
Returns 200 with success even when the id does not exist. Consider returning 404 for non-existent id to make idempotency explicit.
Same as above — no 404 when id does not exist.
Calls 3 external IRMS endpoints sequentially using blocking `requests` lib inside an async route. This blocks the event loop. Use httpx.AsyncClient or run in executor.
Allows changing the PIB to one already used by another company (no duplicate check on update).

action_items: Consider returning 404 (not 200) on DELETE for non-existent company/employee.
Consider switching IRMS lookup from blocking `requests` to async httpx to avoid blocking the event loop.
Add duplicate-PIB check inside PUT /api/companies/{id} (currently only POST checks).
Consider HTTPBearer(auto_error=False) so missing token returns 401 not 403.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: PUT /api/agency was returning 500 due to MongoDB `insert_one` mutating the passed dict with ObjectId `_id`, which then leaked into the response and broke JSON encoding. Fix: pass a copy `dict(doc)` to insert_one (committed in /app/backend/server.py).
Single-file backend server.py is 911 lines — close to the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting routers into /app/backend/routers/{auth,companies,employees,documents,pdv}.py for maintainability.
IRMS lookup uses blocking `requests` in an async endpoint with 8s timeout × 3 endpoints = up to 24s of blocking. Should be async (httpx).

Document download endpoint accepts token via query string and does not validate that the file's company belongs to the authenticated user (currently single-user system so OK, but to be aware for future multi-tenant).

rca of the issue: Bug: PUT /api/agency → 500. RCA: motor's `insert_one(doc)` mutates the dict in place by inserting `_id: ObjectId(...)`. The function then returned that same `doc`, and FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize ObjectId, causing TypeError → 500. Reproduction: GET /api/agency then PUT same body back. Mitigation: pass a shallow copy `dict(doc)` (or `doc.copy()`) to insert_one. Fix applied in server.py line ~298. Verified by re-running pytest — TestAgency::test_update_agency now PASSES.
